spellbook.finance/limitations: Follow the collection-buying skill. Negotiation drafts are not persisted; open begins after both parties have agreed to the recorded terms.

Seller, card, condition, title, payment and refund details are customer-reported or agent-observed evidence. SpellBook does not verify conversations, physical custody, external payments, refund settlement, legal title, or profit.

Only one deal category owns a physical count. Counts and scanCoverage are separate; a repeated image or a bulk count is not a unique-unit scan. Null denominators and missing market values stay unknown.

A deal never creates or changes inventory. Use an existing purchase-incoming/receive workflow only after the goods are accepted, title evidence is recorded, and a person confirms the intake. Returned goods require release evidence.

A rejected estimate can close only as return-only with every received unit released and advances net-refunded. A closed deal needs evidence-backed reopen before late changes. Payment role direction is buyer-to-seller for payment and seller-to-buyer for refund; third-party transfers are outside this ledger.

Market value uses an explicit source, timestamp, quoteCondition and quoteFinish. Unknown bases remain unpriced. A payment without an external reference relies on submitted evidence to identify the transfer.
Submission receipts preserve each command and prior revision. The current snapshot contains bounded evidence; request older revisions by revision number to inspect prior source commands.

description: Record one seller-agreed collection deal or a later receipt, count correction, evaluation, seller response, reported payment/refund, return/title disposition, dispute, closure, or evidence-backed reopening. Read spellbook_skill(name: collection-buying) first. A submission is an immutable, owner-scoped receipt; retry its exact submissionId and payload after an uncertain result. It records evidence only: it does not contact a seller, send money, verify a reported payment, transfer title, receive inventory, or publish cards.
